author: OpenAxolotl maintainer via the project's hero generator
tool: Blender 4.0.2 headless, tools/blender/make_axolotl.py (deterministic), then rigged by tools/rig_model.py. The mesh is built from skin modifiers over edge skeletons plus subdivision, one continuous surface per role (skin, eye, gleam, gill, detail) with named axolotl_<role> materials and vertex-colour albedo. Rigging adds a 12-bone skeleton with weights from inverse-square distance to the two nearest bones, the eye and its highlight bound whole to the head, and six animation clips (idle, waddle, swim, hop, fall, hurt). 29,632 triangles, inside the character budget of 60,000.
prompt: Matched by eye against a reference sheet supplied by the maintainer (2026-09-07): a standing, curious cartoon axolotl — rounded domed head about a quarter of the body, big forward-set dark eyes with catchlights, a wide upturned smile, three feather-shaped coral gill fronds per side held upswept, mottled pale-pink counter-shaded skin, short planted legs with three toes each, and a long tail with a fin ridge sloping down to rest its tip. SUPERSEDES the original upload, a glb from an uncommitted AI-written trimesh script: 85 welded primitives with no generator in the repo. The uploaded reference package's own glb was verified byte-identical to that original upload, so the sheet's textured model was never available as a file; this generator approximates its look in vertex-coloured geometry instead.
